newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil steady in quiet trade.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady at midday on Friday as the market held on to its late week gains in quiet trade, traders said.
"The market is steady after the past two day's bargain hunting but the outlook remains bearish because of the prompt physical overhang," one trader said.
July paper was last quoted at $22.00/$22.20 per barrel, up from late Wednesday's $21.95/$22.65, brokers said.

Traders attributed the firmer prices to a technical rebound with many expecting prices to slip again as a new wave of sellers are anticipated to emerge in the absence of fresh regional enduser demand.
The July swaps traded at a low of $21.60 earlier this week after a new round of physical sellers pushed cash prices down to a traded 20-month low of $21.45 per barrel free-on-board Singapore.

On Thursday a 150,000-barrel cargo traded at $21.60 per barrel fob Singapore for possibly export to China, traders said. The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade remained wide with both July and August bid at about $1.00 per barrel, brokers said, despite the rebound in gas oil prices.
July and August regrade was last quoted at $1.00/$1.30 per barrel, brokers said. July regrade last traded at $1.00 on Wednesday, they said.
Fuel oil swaps was last quoted down due to a weaker physical market where a 20,000 tonne cargo traded at $100.00 per tonne, down $1.50 from Thursday.
July was last quoted at $98.00/$98.75 from $98.50/$99.00, brokers said.
